digest: A database server (FIN-DB-02) was compromised via a malicious Word document launching a hidden PowerShell process. The PowerShell command downloaded and executed a payload from a suspicious external IP (203.0.113.77), which subsequently established persistent command and control communications. This activity was confirmed as unauthorized by the maintenance team.

evidence_findings.title: Malicious PowerShell Execution from Word
evidence_findings.subject: powershell.exe
evidence_findings.evidence: A PowerShell process (`powershell.exe`) was executed on `FIN-DB-02` with a hidden window and an encoded command. The parent process was `winword.exe`. The decoded command `IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient)` was intended to download and execute `hxxps://203.0.113.77/update.dat`.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The execution of PowerShell from `winword.exe` with an encoded command to download and execute an external file is highly indicative of malicious activity, likely initiated by a malicious document or macro.

evidence_findings.title: Unauthorized Command and Control Communication
evidence_findings.evidence: Outbound network connections from `10.20.8.42` (FIN-DB-02) to `203.0.113.77` on port 443 were observed immediately after the PowerShell execution. This destination is not on the corporate allowlist and was receiving periodic connections.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The network connections to `203.0.113.77` correlate directly with the PowerShell activity and represent unauthorized command and control (C2) communication by a compromised host.

evidence_findings.title: Contradiction of Routine Maintenance Claim
evidence_findings.subject: FIN-DB-02
evidence_findings.evidence: The maintenance team explicitly confirmed that no approved work was performed on `FIN-DB-02` that would involve the observed PowerShell command or connections to `203.0.113.77`.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The initial case disposition claiming 'routine maintenance' is false, as confirmed by the responsible team, indicating the activity is unauthorized and malicious.

attack_chain.description: A malicious document (likely via `winword.exe`) was used to gain initial access and execute code on `FIN-DB-02`.
PowerShell was executed on `FIN-DB-02` to download and execute a payload.
The PowerShell process was hidden (`-w hidden`) and the command was encoded (`-enc`) to evade detection.
The compromised host `FIN-DB-02` established persistent outbound communication with `203.0.113.77` on port 443, likely for command and control.

attack_timeline.attack_behavior: Malicious PowerShell execution initiated from winword.exe on FIN-DB-02.
PowerShell attempts to download and execute payload from 203.0.113.77.
Outbound network connections from 10.20.8.42 to 203.0.113.77 observed immediately after PowerShell execution.

ioc_indicators.context: Destination IP for C2 communication and payload download.
URL for the malicious payload download.
Encoded PowerShell command used for execution.
Decoded PowerShell command used for execution.
Parent process of the malicious PowerShell execution, indicating initial access vector.

remediations.description: Immediately isolate FIN-DB-02 (10.20.8.42) from the network to prevent further compromise or data exfiltration.
Perform a full forensic investigation of FIN-DB-02 to identify persistence mechanisms, additional malware, and scope of compromise. Remove all malicious artifacts.
Block IP address 203.0.113.77 at the perimeter firewall and proxy servers to prevent further C2 communication.
Search for similar PowerShell execution patterns, network connections to 203.0.113.77, or `winword.exe` spawning PowerShell across the environment.
Identify the user account associated with the `winword.exe` process and force a password reset. Investigate for potential credential compromise.

unknowns: The specific user account involved in the `winword.exe` execution.
The exact method of initial access (e.g., specific phishing email, exploit kit, or malicious document name).
The full functionality and capabilities of the `update.dat` payload.
The extent of compromise beyond FIN-DB-02 and whether other systems are affected.
